sources.name: ODOT Crash Data System - Decode Database (crash, vehicle, participant tables)

placement_sample.area: Multnomah County (Portland) 2024, ODOT decode DB, TIGER 2024 41051
placement_sample.address_points_source: Oregon Address Points (not needed: no house numbers in ODOT records)

blockers: No licence grant for paid use of ODOT CDS data (disclaimer only)
Decode DB is an Access .mdb: the server needs mdbtools or a pure-Python reader
Freeway crashes need a milepoint tier on ODOT's LRS (not built)
Exact tier 96.6% within 250 ft (low 95.4%) on TIGER-only, below the 98% bar
user_actions: Ask ODOT CAR (ODOTTDSCrashRequestGroup@odot.oregon.gov) for written permission to use CDS data in a paid product
Decide: read the yearly decode DB (persons, 2015-2024) or the ArcGIS layer (crash level, 2019-2024), or both

cities.source: ODOT CDS (no city feed; PBOT defers to ODOT)

manuals.title: ODOT Analysis Procedures Manual v2, Chapter 4 Safety
APM Appendix 4A Crash Attribution and Automation
ODOT HSIP Guide (A Guide to Developing Highway Safety Projects)
Oregon State Highway Crash Rate Tables 2024 (Table II)
Oregon Transportation Safety Action Plan 2021 (crash costs, Table 2)

methods.rates_unit: intersections crashes per MEV (APM Exhibit 4-1, 2003-2007 data, mean + 90th percentile); state-highway segments crashes per MVMT (Crash Rate Table II, 2020-2024)

crash_costs.K: KA combined: urban $1,530,000 interstate / $1,490,000 other state hwy / $1,110,000 off system; rural $2,260,000 / $2,140,000 / $1,940,000

methods.screening_method: SPIS (0.1-mile, 3 years, frequency + rate + severity, top 5%/10%); HSM critical crash rate (P=1.645) on total and F+A crashes; excess proportion of crash types; compare to Exhibit 4-1 90th percentile and Table II
differences_from_ca: Rates: Table II (state highways, per MVMT, urban/rural x functional class) and a per-MEV intersection table with 90th percentiles, instead of TASAS base rates with an ADT factor
Intersections are flagged above the statewide 90th-percentile rate as well as the critical rate
Crash costs combine K+A and B+C by highway type x urban/rural (2019 values); Caltrans LRSM prices KA by location type and B, C, O separately (2026 dollars)
Data window: APM 5 years recommended, SIM 3 years, SPIS 3 years, ARTS 5 years
Screening is SPIS, ODOT's own 0.1-mile method
Oregon publishes HSM calibration factors (APM Exhibit 4-11); freeway/ISATe uncalibrated
Self-reporting state, PDO threshold $2,500: PDO-based rates are not comparable to California
